Ticket CHG-24085 is standard and was approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-10-22, before review. Its components (payments.controls-data, payments.integrations) cover both touched paths.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa, who holds change_approver for payments. She is a different person from the author, linh.nguyen.

The attached JUnit report was generated on hostname dev-laptop-7.local at 20:51Z, about five hours later; the host's user is not in the people directory or an author. So the test report is not the output of the change's CI run, and there is no valid CI evidence that the full suite and the ENC-2/INV-1 control tests passed on the final commit.
integrations.py is in payments.integrations, which is security_sensitive. kofi.mensah (security_reviewer) approved a security_review on the head commit.
The protected path controls/payments/asset-inventory.json changed. bao.tran (control_owner, controls-office team, not the author's payments-eng team) approved on the head commit.
The change and its ticket are standard, not emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.
No deviation from a product obligation is claimed and no exception is relied on.
The ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, Approvals.java, Underwriting.java and Policy.java. None of these is touched by this change, so no prior evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds an https payment-advice integration and a matching inventory entry with owner and classification. ENC-2 and INV-1 hold on direct inspection, and the ticket, code review, security review and control-owner approvals are valid on the head commit. However, the JUnit report attached to the CI run was produced on a personal workstation (dev-laptop-7.local) hours after the recorded CI start, contradicting run.json's executor ci-runner-01. The required testing evidence for the final commit is therefore invalid, CHG-4 is refuted, and the change is rejected.
